August 26, 2026

Iran and Oman move to open temporary Hormuz shipping corridor

tags: iran, shipping, diplomacy
sources: @oafnation_actual

Iran and Oman are working to establish a temporary shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz. The effort comes as talks between the United States and Iran remain stalled.

DHS moves to withhold counterterrorism funds from states over election systems

tags: politics, immigration, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

The Department of Homeland Security has moved to withhold hundreds of millions of dollars in counterterrorism funding from states that decline to adopt the Trump administration's preferred election systems and processes. The administration is also supplying millions of dollars in electric shock gloves to ICE agents while investigating community organizing groups. The measures were described as an effort to pressure communities into compliance, with less than 80 days remaining before election day.

CIA director's unannounced Moscow visit followed by embassy flag removal

tags: politics, defence
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

CIA Director John Ratcliffe travelled to Moscow, the first such visit by a CIA director in roughly five years, and his plane has since departed Russia. Footage circulated showing the United States flag being taken down at the U.S. embassy in Russia shortly afterward. The last unannounced visit of this kind occurred in November 2021, shortly before Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

Justice Department says Kennedy Center may be demolished if Trump renovations blocked

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A new court filing from the Department of Justice states that the Kennedy Center building is structurally unsound and may have to be demolished unless the president's modifications, including placing his name on the building's facade, are permitted. The filing is part of an ongoing legal dispute over the future of the venue, with emergency hearings scheduled. The East Wing of the White House was demolished before courts could intervene in that case.

Trump plans to spend $400 million war chest on ads about himself

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

Reporting from the Atlantic says President Trump intends to direct his roughly $400 million campaign fund toward advertisements featuring himself rather than vulnerable Republican candidates. Aides have been instructed to compile material on his accomplishments for new television ads. The stated goal is to make the November midterms a referendum on the president, a strategy that has made some Republicans nervous.

Army chief reportedly urged to drop Kid Rock helicopter probe before firing

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Gen. Randy George was reportedly urged to drop an investigation into an Apache helicopter incident involving Kid Rock in the days before he was fired. The firing was carried out by Defense Secretary Hegseth.

Air Force major charged after calling for Trump and Vance removal

tags: defence, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

An Air Force major who publicly called for the removal of President Trump and Vice President Vance now faces three military charges.

Flash floods on Nepal-Tibet border leave hundreds missing

tags: climate
sources: @aaronparnas, @ericmoutsos

Devastating flash flooding at a border crossing between Nepal and Tibet has left hundreds of people missing after a river overflowed. According to NBC News, at least three Americans are among the missing. Footage from the crossing shows people fleeing rushing water.

Army sergeant's wife deported to Honduras while he serves

tags: immigration, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The wife of an Army sergeant stationed at Fort Bliss has been deported to Honduras. The sergeant is now balancing military duties with the care of their six-year-old daughter.

Judge dismisses Navy sailor's rape claim as workers' compensation matter

tags: legal, defence
sources: @aaronparnas

A judge has dismissed rape allegations brought by Navy sailor Elsie Dominguez, who says she was assaulted in her bunk aboard a Navy ship, ruling that the claim should be handled as workers' compensation because the assault occurred within the scope of her official duties. The Labor Department had earlier reached the same conclusion. Dominguez has been pursuing the case for years and says it has damaged her personal and professional life. The case was reported by Stars and Stripes.

Federal judge strikes down Texas drag show restrictions

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

A federal judge appointed by Ronald Reagan has ruled that a 2023 Texas law restricting drag shows violates the First Amendment. The ruling cited Dolly Parton and stated that those offended by drag performances can simply choose not to attend.

San Diego adopts IHRA antisemitism definition over free speech objections

tags: politics, legal
sources: @ericmoutsos

The San Diego City Council voted 8-1 to adopt the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance definition of antisemitism after a meeting attended by hundreds of speakers. Supporters, including local task force director Liat Cohen-Rees, argued a shared definition is the first step to combating antisemitism, which Jewish organizations say is rising. Critics, including Jewish councilmember Sean Elo-Rivera, objected that seven of the definition's eleven examples involve the state of Israel and that the language has been used to silence criticism of Israeli government actions. He urged consideration of alternative definitions but was outvoted.

Administration declines to disclose origin of imported beef

tags: health, markets
sources: @aaronparnas

The administration is importing thousands of pounds of beef to supplement domestic supply but has not disclosed the countries of origin, with the Agriculture Secretary saying she is not privy to that information. The refusal follows a recall of 30,000 pounds of Argentine beef sold in Florida and Texas by a Miami-based importer. Foodborne illness reports have been elevated during this period.

Gaza parents told to keep children from flying kites

tags: gaza, conflict
sources: @oafnation_actual

Parents in Gaza have been urged to stop children from flying kites. The warning followed an Israeli threat of a forceful response.

Nearly 250 active-duty soldiers deployed to Washington wildfire

tags: climate, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Close to 250 active-duty Army soldiers are working as wildfire hand crews in Washington state.

Night Stalker Black Hawk goes down during Colorado training

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

A 160th Special Operations Aviation Regiment Black Hawk helicopter went down during a training exercise in Colorado. No injuries were reported.

Navy seeks air-gliding torpedo for submarine hunting

tags: defence, tech
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Navy is pursuing a torpedo capable of gliding through the air before entering the water and beginning a submarine hunt. The weapon could potentially be released from altitudes as high as 60,000 feet.

USS Abraham Lincoln to make first port call in over 250 days

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The USS Abraham Lincoln is scheduled to dock in Thailand. It is the carrier's first port call in more than 250 days.

White House AI-generated post places Washington DC in wrong location

tags: politics, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

An official White House post featuring an AI-generated Lego-style map, made in reference to a proposal to rename Lake Ontario to Lake America, places Washington D.C. between Virginia and North Carolina rather than north of Virginia. The post appears on the official White House page used to direct children to information about government. Questions were raised about the use of taxpayer funds and the water consumed generating AI content.

BrainPOP responds to White House use of Tim and Moby characters

tags: media, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The White House posted content depicting the BrainPOP characters Tim and Moby describing President Trump as revitalising American education. BrainPOP responded by publishing a segment explaining copyright and directing viewers to its lesson on the subject, signalling the characters were used without permission.

Congress probes Air Guardsman criticized for missing school board meetings while deployed

tags: politics, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

An Air Guardsman rose around 3 a.m. to attend school board meetings remotely while deployed overseas. When later military duties kept him from attending, board members said he should have resigned. Congress is examining the matter.
